content.user_title: Build Modern React and Next.js Interfaces
content.value_statement: Complex frontend work requires coordinated decisions across architecture, state, accessibility, testing, and performance. This skill provides implementation guidance for modern React and Next.js projects.
actual_capabilities: Build React 19 components with Server Components, Suspense, Actions, and advanced hooks.
Structure Next.js 15 applications with App Router, streaming, route handlers, and rendering strategies.
Plan client and server state using React Query, SWR, Zustand, Jotai, or Redux Toolkit.
Create responsive interfaces with modern CSS, Tailwind CSS, design tokens, and component libraries.
Improve accessibility, Core Web Vitals, bundle size, loading behavior, and error handling.
Design component, end-to-end, visual regression, performance, and accessibility testing workflows.
limitations: The skill does not replace testing in the target browser, device, deployment environment, or assistive technology.
Backend-only architecture, native application development, and visual design without implementation are outside its primary scope.
Recommendations require project requirements, framework versions, browser targets, and performance goals for accurate implementation.
Third-party integrations still require current vendor documentation, credentials, security review, and environment-specific configuration.

use_cases.title: Build a Product Interface
use_cases.description: Create responsive React screens with typed components, loading states, accessible interactions, and maintainable styling.

use_cases.title: Plan a Next.js Architecture
use_cases.description: Choose rendering, routing, data fetching, caching, and state patterns for a new application.

use_cases.title: Improve Web Quality
use_cases.description: Audit an existing interface for accessibility, rendering performance, Core Web Vitals, and testing gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a React Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a React component for [feature]. Use TypeScript, responsive styling, keyboard support, loading states, and clear prop definitions.

prompt_templates.title: Design an App Router Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Next.js App Router page for [workflow]. Explain server and client boundaries, data fetching, caching, errors, and metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component or page] for unnecessary rendering, bundle cost, accessibility, and Core Web Vitals. Prioritize changes and define verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Frontend Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a frontend architecture for [product]. Cover routing, rendering, state, design systems, testing, observability, deployment constraints, and migration risks.

output_examples.input: Plan an accessible account settings form with optimistic updates.
output: A component boundary plan for server data, form state, and mutation feedback.
Accessible labels, validation messages, focus handling, and keyboard behavior.
Pending, success, rollback, and error states with focused test cases.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow Next.js product page.
output: A prioritized review of rendering, image loading, fonts, scripts, caching, and bundle size.
Recommended measurements for LCP, CLS, interaction latency, and route payloads.
Specific optimization steps with expected impact and regression checks.

output_examples.input: Choose state management for a collaborative dashboard.
output: A separation of server cache, local interface state, form state, and real-time updates.
A library recommendation based on synchronization, complexity, and team constraints.
A conflict handling strategy with optimistic updates and recovery behavior.

best_practices: Provide framework versions, browser targets, target devices, data contracts, and measurable success criteria.
Request accessibility, loading, error, empty, and responsive states as part of the initial implementation.
Validate generated guidance with type checks, automated tests, browser profiling, and real device review.
anti_patterns: Do not request isolated visual components without data behavior, interaction states, or accessibility requirements.
Do not apply performance optimizations before measuring rendering, network, and bundle behavior.
Do not accept framework recommendations without checking project constraints, current documentation, and deployment compatibility.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on React 19, Next.js 15, TypeScript, modern CSS, and common React ecosystem tools.

faq.question: Can it build accessible interfaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers semantic HTML, ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, focus management, contrast, forms, and accessibility testing.

faq.question: Can it improve frontend performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses rendering, code splitting, images, fonts, caching, bundles, Core Web Vitals, and profiling.

faq.question: Does it support application state and data fetching?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers React Query, SWR, Zustand, Jotai, Valtio, Redux Toolkit, Context, WebSockets, and optimistic updates.

faq.question: Does it replace project testing?
faq.answer: No. Generated work still requires type checks, automated tests, browser validation, accessibility review, and deployment verification.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the user workflow, framework version, existing code, data contracts, design constraints, browser targets, and acceptance criteria.
